output.brief: The most likely cause is contaminated brake fluid, not driver technique or the new pads. All 11 Eastgate vans with soft-pedal complaints were serviced at Northfield Motor Services while the in-house bay was closed. Northfield used an old bulk drum with a missing cap that had taken on water. Two vans that got fluid from a fresh sealed drum had no complaints. Two vans (LK-217, LK-224) tested at 149–152°C boiling point, against 255°C for sealed stock. Renewing their fluid is recorded in the Northfield warranty card. Northfield recommended rechecking the other vans on 25 Sep, and nobody replied. The same drivers had no problems in other vans on the same hilly routes. Calder Road vans fitted with the same Tessaro pads show no complaints. I'm fairly sure of this, though I haven't tested the other 11 vans' fluid directly. Next steps: take all 13 Northfield-serviced vans off the road until their fluid is tested and renewed from sealed stock. Check Calder Road's fluid source too. Do not discipline drivers, because they reported a real safety fault. Hold off on changing pad supplier until there is evidence about the pads.
